_comment: ESP-Hosted test catalogue — vision-first. Every element is an entity with properties; behaviour is defined by props, not by type. A scenario = one emulator run (build cp@C6 + host@P4, launch the bench, drive stimulus, capture serial). Its cases = named assertions on that run: each case must see every `expect` substring and must NOT see any `absent` (crash) marker within `timeout_s`. positive vs negative is just the `kind` property — the assertion engine is identical (a negative case simply expects the graceful-failure line). `support` gates execution: supported runs; unsupported/tbd are catalogued but skipped with a reason. The example tree seeds the BASE (minimal) scenario set; further scenarios are derived from the codebase's own behaviours and error paths (lifecycle, transport-integrity, rpc, capabilities, security) — what SHOULD be tested, not only what is runnable today. This file is the single source of truth for both the CLI runner and the UI.

p4_c6_sdio.label: ESP32-P4 host ⇄ ESP32-C6 coprocessor (SDIO)
p4_c6_sdio.notes: The canonical hosted bench: SDIO bridge over a Unix socket, P4→C6 reset on GPIO 54, C6→P4 host-wakeup on GPIO 2, NAT'd networking with a built-in AP (myssid/mypassword).
